warnings: 2 assumptions feed no figure on any screen: empirical_bayes_min_card_pop, relief_scenario

assumptions.description: Multiplier applied to P(10) taken from a population report, with the removed mass reassigned to P(9). Population reports count cards people CHOSE to submit after pre-screening, so P(10 | submitted) overstates P(10 | this card in my hands). Applied once, never twice.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Log every card actually submitted and its result. After ~30 submissions, realised P(10) divided by the population gem rate is the number. Split by game and era before trusting it.

assumptions.description: P(10 | the card is already in a PSA 9 slab) with no condition read supplied. NOT the base gem rate: PSA examined this card and declined a 10, so the base rate double-counts information the grader already acted on. Deliberately conservative so the model discourages resubmission by default.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Log every 9 resubmitted and its outcome. This calibrates slowly because few are submitted; until n>=20 treat the default as a floor, not an estimate.

assumptions.description: P(a resubmitted 9 comes back below 9). Non-zero by construction: a different grader on a different day can see the card less generously, and the original slab no longer exists in that branch.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Same submission log as regrade_conditional_prior; count downgrades separately.

assumptions.description: Multipliers applied to regrade_conditional_prior once the user supplies a complete condition read (centering, corners, surface, edges). Absent a complete read, Model B returns a refusal rather than a number.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Requires outcome data segmented by condition read, which needs a larger submission log than the base prior. Lowest-priority calibration.

assumptions.description: Per-set hit rates per pack, by rarity band, feeding Model E. Community-sourced: self-reported, survivorship-biased toward posted hits, and usually quoted without a denominator. Model E stamps every result low-confidence and the flag cannot be turned off.
assumptions.unit: map of set -> rarity band -> probability per pack
assumptions.calibration_plan: Only your own opened-product log produces a trustworthy number, and the sample needed is larger than you will ever open. Treat Model E rankings as indicative and its magnitudes as unreliable, permanently.

assumptions.description: Which fee schedule applies per venue, and the assumption that the schedule in config/fees.yaml matches what is actually charged. Fees are banded, apply to different bases per venue (eBay charges on item + shipping + tax), and change without notice.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Reconcile against a real settled payout every quarter: take one actual sale, compute the expected fee from config, compare to what was withheld. A discrepancy means the schedule moved.

assumptions.description: Grader tier fees, minimums and turnarounds, and the assumption that config/grading.yaml still matches the grader's own page. PSA paused its four Value tiers on 2026-06-02 against a backlog reported near 10M cards, with no reinstatement date, and Regular turnaround running 40-60 business days. This must live in dated config, never in code -- anything hardcoded is already wrong.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Re-read each grader's own pricing page quarterly and on any announcement. PSA entries carry needs_primary_verification because secondary sources disagree on Value tier pricing, backlog size and membership cost.

assumptions.description: Beta-Binomial prior strength in pseudo-cards: how many set-level observations the prior is worth when shrinking a single card's population distribution toward its set. Materially moves P(10) for thin-population cards, which moves the break-even probability.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Backtest shrinkage strength against realised grade outcomes once the submission log exists. Until then this is a modelling choice, not a measurement.

assumptions.description: Below this total population, a card's own grade distribution is ignored entirely and the set-level distribution is used. Stops a card with 3 tens out of 4 graded from implying a 75% gem rate.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Sensitivity-test the threshold against the same outcome log; the right value is where out-of-sample error stops improving.

assumptions.description: Expected days from listing to settled sale. Feeds annualised ROI together with grading turnaround; a wrong value rescales every annualised figure in the app.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Measure directly from your own sales: median days from list to payout, per venue. This is the easiest entry here to calibrate and should be done first.

assumptions.description: Tax on acquiring the card, by BUY ROUTE. Not a single rate: a UK second-hand purchase carries none I can reclaim or see, an import over 135 carries VAT and duty, an import at or under 135 has VAT collected by the marketplace at the point of sale and no duty, and buying in China or Japan while I am there carries neither.
assumptions.current_value: {"uk_domestic_secondhand": {"vat_pct": 0.0, "duty_pct": 0.0, "note": "margin scheme; VAT embedded, not reclaimable"}, "import_to_uk_over_135": {"vat_pct": 0.2, "duty_pct": 0.02, "note": "compounds: duty on goods+freight, VAT on goods+freight+duty"}, "import_to_uk_at_or_under_135": {"vat_pct": 0.2, "duty_pct": 0.0, "note": "VAT collected at point of sale by the marketplace"}, "cn_jp_domestic": {"vat_pct": 0.0, "duty_pct": 0.0, "note": "bought in country, carried back"}}
assumptions.calibration_plan: confirm the 135 threshold treatment on a real import

assumptions.description: Minimum graded sale comps in the window before a card may appear in a screen. Model D suppresses any card where either grade's sample is below it. A screen built on three sales is noise wearing a suit.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Methodology floor rather than a market observation, so it has a real default. Revisit only if the suppressed fraction of the universe proves unworkable -- and measure that fraction before changing it.

assumptions.description: Which FX reference rate is authoritative, and the assumption that a daily reference rate is close enough to the rate actually realised on conversion. Every converted amount stores the rate used and that rate's as-of date.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Compare the stored rate against the rate actually received on a real conversion, quarterly. The gap is fx_conversion_spread, not error.

assumptions.description: Spread paid on an actual currency conversion, over and above the reference rate, and separate from a marketplace's own conversion charge. Zero is a valid value and must be entered as 0.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Read off a real conversion: (rate received / reference rate) - 1.

assumptions.description: Which customs relief applies when a graded card is returned from a US grader to the UK. relief_none charges 20% VAT plus 2% duty on the full declared value of the GRADED card; relief_rgr zeroes it; relief_opr charges only on the value added. Returned Goods Relief requires the goods to come back unaltered and not upgraded to increase their value, and grading is arguably exactly that. HMRC publishes no card-specific guidance. Outward Processing Relief needs authorisation about thirty working days BEFORE export, so it is not available for a one-off.
assumptions.calibration_plan: Ask a customs broker, or run one low-value submission and read the C88 on the return leg. Until then relief_none is the assumption because it is the realistic outcome for an unprepared private sender -- and because being wrong in that direction costs nothing, while assuming relief and not getting it costs 22.4% of the card.

fee_schedules.summary: 13.25% on item + shipping + tax; $0.30 under $10 / $0.40 over; half rate at or above $1000 up to $7500, 2.35% above
10% + 2.9% + $0.50; fee base not stated by the source
